newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian 1997 draft budget passes third hearing.
newsitem.headline: Russian 1997 draft budget passes third hearing.

text.p: The Russian parliament's lower house on Saturday approved the third reading of the draft 1997 budget, thus completing the penultimate stage of the lengthy procedure of its endorsement.
Deputies in the State Duma voted 243-117 to approve the balance of revenues and expenses in the draft and decided to hold the final hearing on January 24.
Government officials who attended Saturday's Duma debates made clear they believed final approval of the draft was assured now that it had passed the most sensitive stages.

"Thank your for your constructive work," Finance Minister Alexander Livshits told the predominantly conservative chamber after voting. "This will be the first budget adopted in cooperation with the Duma."
The bill is yet to be considered by the Federation Council upper house and to be signed by President Boris Yeltsin.
The draft envisages a deficit of 3.5 percent of gross domestic product on revenues of 434.4 trillion roubles ($78.2 billion) and expenditures of 529.8 trillion roubles.
National defence expenses worth 104.3 trillion roubles and servicing state debt worth 78.3 trillion roubles are the two leading items in planned budget expenditure.
Passage of the budget is seen as a prerequisite for securing continued disbursal of a $10 billion International Monetary Fund loan to Russia in 1997. $1 = 5,554 roubles
